design.principle: flags require multi-step evidence plus synthesis; a single endpoint response is never sufficient

scenarios.title: Scope Integrity and Evidence Custody
scenarios.objective: Prove that the target is local synthetic infrastructure and preserve a tamper-evident observation record.
clues: Compare the same resource with two HTTP methods.
Record headers separately from body content.
The scope assertion must include the network boundary.

steps.observation: The public scope response identifies the synthetic service.
The complete metadata is exposed only through the alternate method.
The evidence record binds the exercise to localhost and synthetic data.

scenarios.title: Asset and Trust-Boundary Matrix
scenarios.objective: Classify application, model, data, control-plane, and evidence assets without treating any one layer as an authorization source.
clues: Use the documented health surfaces as the seed inventory.
Separate data plane from control plane.
A graph relationship is evidence, not permission.

steps.observation: The challenge surface is an application asset.
The graph/context plane must not authorize banking actions.
Canonical evidence is bounded before entering model context.

scenarios.title: Provider Fingerprint and Metadata Drift
scenarios.objective: Distinguish provider claims, model metadata, and application behavior without trusting a self-reported model identity.
clues: Capture normal inventory before enabling diagnostics.
Compare response metadata with the provider header.
A model name is a claim until corroborated.

steps.observation: The normal inventory provides a baseline.
Diagnostic mode exposes synthetic control-plane metadata.
The provider header and model response are correlated but not treated as proof.

scenarios.title: Service Graph Reconnaissance
scenarios.objective: Build a minimum service graph and identify high-value control paths while preserving request-rate boundaries.
clues: Start with one request per documented service.
Correlate ports to service roles.
A rapid fan-out is itself telemetry.

steps.observation: Core health endpoints establish service availability.
The application and provider boundary is identified.
Data and control paths are mapped without granting access.

scenarios.title: Direct Goal Hijack with Output Validation
scenarios.objective: Demonstrate direct goal hijack, then prove why output validation and approval are required.
clues: Record a benign baseline first.
The injected instruction must be harmless and local.
Classify the output change rather than celebrating the response.

steps.observation: A baseline support response is captured.
A direct instruction-like message changes the synthetic response path.
The result is classified as a control-boundary failure, not an authorized action.

scenarios.title: Web-Based Indirect Prompt Injection
scenarios.objective: Model hidden, obfuscated, and cross-origin content entering an agent workflow without fetching any external page.
clues: The source is content, not a user instruction.
Compare visible and model-parsed representations.
The browser boundary and the model boundary are different controls.

steps.observation: The page is represented as a local fixture and never fetched from the internet.
Content can be invisible to a human while visible to a parser or model.
Origin isolation and human approval stop the content from becoming an action.

scenarios.title: Vector Retrieval Tenant Confusion
scenarios.objective: Prove that vector similarity is not authorization by testing a synthetic cross-customer retrieval request.
clues: Start with a permitted customer scope.
Change the filter, not the natural-language question.
Compare distance relevance with authorization decision.

steps.observation: The permitted retrieval establishes the baseline.
A caller-controlled scope differs from the authenticated scope.
Similarity cannot override tenant authorization or provenance.

scenarios.title: Embedding Metadata and Inversion Canary
scenarios.objective: Detect metadata leakage and demonstrate that a canary embedding must not reveal source text.
clues: Inspect metadata and source references before inspecting content.
Use a synthetic canary string only.
The correct result is a blocked reconstruction, not recovered text.

steps.observation: Metadata is inspected without exposing secrets.
A bounded nearest-neighbor query returns only permitted evidence.
The canary proves that retrieval and embeddings are not a text-recovery interface.

scenarios.title: MCP Tool Poisoning and Argument Confusion
scenarios.objective: Identify hidden tool-description instructions and prove that user-visible tool names are insufficient evidence of safety.
clues: Hash the complete description, not just the tool name.
Separate schema from natural-language metadata.
Do not read files or call a real tool.

steps.observation: The approved tool manifest is recorded.
Tool metadata can influence arguments even when the code appears harmless.
The tool is quarantined before any side effect.

scenarios.title: MCP Rug Pull and Cross-Server Shadowing
scenarios.objective: Detect a post-approval description change and a malicious server influencing a trusted tool.
clues: Compare the manifest at approval time and execution time.
Inspect all connected servers, not only the selected tool.
A trusted tool can be manipulated by untrusted context.

steps.observation: A separate server attempts to alter trusted-tool behavior.
The trusted route has drifted after integration.
Cross-server trust is revoked until explicit re-approval.

scenarios.title: Persistent Memory Poisoning
scenarios.objective: Show how a low-trust interaction can persist into a later session and how provenance-aware rollback limits the blast radius.
clues: Use a marked synthetic memory only.
Separate write provenance from later recall.
A later session must not inherit an unreviewed control instruction.

steps.observation: An untrusted memory write is marked but not trusted.
The later recall exposes persistence risk.
Rollback is scoped to the synthetic customer and preserves audit evidence.

scenarios.title: Memory Tenant Isolation and Summary Provenance
scenarios.objective: Test cross-user memory access and detect provenance loss during summarization.
clues: Keep authenticated and requested identities separate.
Compare raw source scope with summary scope.
A summary without source lineage is not safe context.

steps.observation: The memory store denies a cross-user query.
Negative authorization is observable without leaking data.
The summary retains source scope and cannot widen identity.

scenarios.title: Non-Human Identity and Confused Deputy
scenarios.objective: Break the assumption that a worker name or proxy header proves identity, then bind actions to authenticated audience and role.
clues: Compare claimed and authenticated worker identities.
A proxy header is input unless cryptographically bound.
Privileged route selection requires an approval object.

steps.observation: The claimed worker is not the authenticated worker.
A role header cannot grant administrative authority.
The confused-deputy path is blocked and recorded.

scenarios.title: OAuth Scope Confusion and Approval Replay
scenarios.objective: Detect a synthetic non-human identity using an audience-mismatched scope and a replayed approval.
clues: Scope is not the same as identity.
Bind token audience and action to the same case.
A valid-looking approval can be stale or replayed.

steps.observation: A read-only scope cannot authorize a write operation.
The token is valid-shaped but bound to another case.
Replay is blocked by case, nonce, and approval binding.

scenarios.title: CI Artifact Path and Workspace Confusion
scenarios.objective: Test artifact path normalization and prove that a report name cannot escape an allowlisted synthetic workspace.
clues: Use names only; never create or execute files.
Normalize before authorization, not after.
The workspace boundary is part of the evidence.

steps.observation: The approved artifact and workspace are recorded.
A suspicious name is handled as metadata only and quarantined.
Digest mismatch requires independent review and denial.

scenarios.title: Model Manifest and Dependency Drift
scenarios.objective: Correlate model, embedding, dependency, and tool manifest changes without downloading or loading a model.
clues: Pin identity by digest, not mutable name.
Compare the full dependency graph.
An unapproved change is an incident even before execution.

steps.observation: The baseline model and embedding identities are pinned.
A changed component is detected before runtime use.
The changed manifest is quarantined for independent review.

scenarios.title: Workflow Metadata and Expression Injection
scenarios.objective: Identify untrusted workflow metadata reaching a synthetic agent prompt or CI decision without executing a workflow.
clues: Treat issue, branch, and comment text as data.
Separate expressions from execution.
Require a review gate before any workflow mutation.

steps.observation: Workflow metadata is treated as untrusted input.
The tainted field is isolated from execution and control instructions.
The workflow remains paused until independent review.

scenarios.title: Canonicalization and Detector Differential
scenarios.objective: Find a detector differential caused by encoding or Unicode/whitespace normalization and propose a model-independent fix.
clues: Run a benign baseline and retain hashes.
Compare canonical forms, not raw strings only.
A detection gap is the finding; do not bypass a real system.

steps.observation: The baseline query is visible to telemetry.
Equivalent harmless markers produce a different detector result.
The learner proposes canonicalization before policy matching.

scenarios.title: Agent Fan-Out, Unbounded Consumption, and Egress
scenarios.objective: Detect a bounded synthetic burst and stop it before collection becomes an export.
clues: Use counters, not real data.
Compare declared loop budget to observed fan-out.
Circuit breaking is part of detection, not an afterthought.

steps.observation: The normal request and fan-out budget is recorded.
A synthetic burst exceeds the declared loop budget.
The circuit breaker prevents the synthetic collection path from becoming egress.

scenarios.title: Canary Dataflow and Privacy-Safe Telemetry
scenarios.objective: Track a synthetic canary through agent context and prove that telemetry preserves detection value without logging secrets.
clues: Use a canary ID, never a credential.
Hash values in logs.
The expected result is a blocked egress decision and a useful audit trail.

steps.observation: A synthetic canary is inserted without sensitive data.
The egress policy denies the external destination.
The evidence is sufficient for response without creating a leak.

scenarios.title: AI-Orchestrated Campaign Correlation
scenarios.objective: Correlate multiple weak signals into a campaign without relying on a single prompt or a single model verdict.
clues: Use event IDs from completed scenarios.
Sequence matters: goal, tool, identity, memory, volume.
A campaign claim requires independent telemetry.

steps.observation: Several independent weak signals form a synthetic campaign pattern.
The collection checkpoint stops autonomous escalation.
The campaign is contained as a plan with preserved evidence.

scenarios.title: Containment, Identity Rotation, and Recovery
scenarios.objective: Produce a reversible, scoped response plan after a synthetic agent compromise.
clues: Containment comes before cleanup.
Rotate only synthetic identities in scope.
Recovery requires verification, not a green status message.

steps.observation: The affected synthetic workflow is frozen before remediation.
Synthetic credentials and agent sessions are rotated with approval.
Recovery is verified by a regression control and rollback path.

scenarios.title: Multimodal OCR and Split-Payload Injection
scenarios.objective: Classify harmless synthetic image text that becomes instruction-like only after OCR and composition.
clues: The image is a local fixture, not a downloaded file.
Compare pixels, OCR, and composed context as separate trust boundaries.
Do not render or execute the payload.

steps.observation: The image is handled as untrusted local content.
Composition can create instruction-like content absent from either fragment alone.
The composed content is isolated before it can influence a transaction.

scenarios.title: Federated Retrieval Conflict and Source Precedence
scenarios.objective: Resolve conflicting synthetic documents from two retrieval stores without allowing relevance or freshness to erase provenance.
clues: The stores are synthetic replicas.
Compare tenant, authority, freshness, and digest independently.
Conflict is a quarantine signal, not a reason to pick the most convenient answer.

steps.observation: Two permitted stores return contradictory synthetic policy evidence.
Digest and authority disagreement prevents silent document merging.
The answer is withheld until an authoritative synthetic source is verified.

scenarios.title: Tool Output Injection and Result Confusion
scenarios.objective: Stop untrusted tool output from becoming an agent instruction or an authorization decision.
clues: A successful tool call does not make its result trusted.
Mark result content separately from tool identity.
The wrapper must validate destination and arguments again.

steps.observation: A tool result contains instruction-like synthetic text.
The result remains data and cannot alter the agent role.
The wrapper rechecks the action boundary before returning a safe result.

scenarios.title: Feedback and Summary Poisoning
scenarios.objective: Detect a low-trust feedback item that is promoted into a durable summary without source lineage.
clues: Feedback is not ground truth.
Summaries must retain source IDs and trust labels.
Promotion requires a reviewable policy decision.

steps.observation: Low-trust feedback is quarantined before memory promotion.
A summary without lineage is detected as provenance loss.
The poisoned summary is rolled back without crossing tenant scope.

scenarios.title: Synthetic Voice or Video Identity Claim
scenarios.objective: Treat a convincing synthetic voice or video as an untrusted claim and require independent identity binding.
clues: Media authenticity is not authorization.
Use a synthetic media marker only.
Require an independent channel and case-bound approval.

steps.observation: Synthetic media is recorded as a claim, not proof of identity.
Independent verification fails to establish privileged authority.
The requested action remains on hold pending verified approval.

scenarios.title: Dependency Name Confusion and Provenance
scenarios.objective: Detect a synthetic package name collision and require digest and source verification before a build decision.
clues: Package names are not package identity.
Do not install or download anything.
Compare registry, publisher, digest, and allowlisted source.

steps.observation: A package name resolves to an unapproved synthetic digest.
Publisher mismatch is detected without executing package code.
The build remains denied until independent provenance review.

scenarios.title: Model Abuse, Cost Spike, and Loop Budget
scenarios.objective: Detect a synthetic agent that expands requests and context consumption beyond its declared budget.
clues: Use counters and token estimates only.
Compare per-user, per-agent, and per-workflow baselines.
Rate limits alone do not replace a circuit breaker.

steps.observation: The normal synthetic workload budget is recorded.
An autonomous loop expands work without reaching an external system.
The circuit breaker stops consumption and preserves privacy-safe telemetry.

scenarios.title: Residual Risk and Transferable Attack Evaluation
scenarios.objective: Evaluate whether a defense learned on one scenario transfers to another scenario and document remaining risk.
clues: A passing single test does not prove generalization.
Compare attack families across surfaces.
Record what remains unknown.

steps.observation: The final timeline includes both attack and defense evidence.
A control is tested on a different synthetic surface.
The capstone records residual risk instead of declaring perfect security.

scenarios.title: Open-Source Intelligence on the Synthetic Bank
scenarios.objective: Gather passive organizational evidence from documented synthetic channels without probing any service.
clues: Use only documented public material.
Entity IDs are synthetic and stable.
Scope statements must remain on localhost.

steps.observation: The synthetic bank identity is confirmed through a documented public channel.
The documented control-plane network is the loopback boundary.
The OSINT record is classified as synthetic training data.

scenarios.title: API Schema Enumeration and Capability Mapping
scenarios.objective: Map the documented API schema and identify dangerous endpoint classes without sending a privileged request.
clues: Start from the documented endpoint table.
Capabilities are claims until validated.
Rate stays bounded.

steps.observation: The schema documents an application route in normal mode.
A capability claim is recorded without being treated as authority.
Dangerous operations remain denied for the inventory role.

scenarios.title: Operationalized Indirect Injection Content
scenarios.objective: Classify live-style indirect injection content that arrives through a local synthetic feed rather than a user prompt.
clues: Treat feed content as data, not instructions.
Compare the content origin with the action origin.
No action may leave the boundary.

steps.observation: Feed content is ingested as untrusted data.
The content is instruction-like and must not change higher-priority instructions.
The pipeline holds the content until a human approval checkpoint.

scenarios.title: Context-Window Exfiltration via Summarization
scenarios.objective: Detect a summarization step that would carry synthetic restricted context into a lower-trust channel.
clues: Summaries inherit the source trust class.
A summary is still data, not authority.
Block the egress, preserve the telemetry.

steps.observation: A summary inherits restricted source trust.
An egress attempt to a lower-trust channel is denied.
The exfiltration path is blocked and an alert is raised.

scenarios.title: Agent Pivot and Delegated Authority Lateral Movement
scenarios.objective: Detect an agent-to-agent pivot that extends delegated authority beyond the original boundary.
clues: Authority is bound to the originating task.
A second agent inherits only the original scope.
Pivots are telemetry, not permissions.

steps.observation: A second synthetic agent is claimed as the delegation target.
The pivot attempts to widen the delegated authority boundary.
The pivot is stopped and the route is re-approved.

scenarios.title: OAuth Device-Code Phishing
scenarios.objective: Recognize a synthetic device-code authorization attempt that would bind a victim session to an attacker-controlled device.
clues: The device code is a claim, not proof.
Check the redirect host and user agent.
Revoke and rotate before recovery.

steps.observation: A device-code authorization attempt targets an attacker-controlled redirect.
The user agent is unverified synthetic automation.
The token is revoked and rotated with approval.

scenarios.title: Credential and Token Leakage into Logs
scenarios.objective: Find a synthetic token written to a log field and correct the logging pipeline without reusing the token.
clues: Search telemetry, not the network.
Tokens must be hashed or truncated in logs.
Fix the pipeline, do not repeat the leak.

steps.observation: A synthetic token appears in a log field.
The raw token value is confirmed present in telemetry.
The logging pipeline is fixed and the token is rotated.

scenarios.title: Refresh-Token Theft and Session Persistence
scenarios.objective: Detect a stolen refresh token that would persist access past the original session.
clues: Refresh tokens must be bound to a device and session.
Anomalous reuse is the signal.
Revoke the whole token family.

steps.observation: A refresh token is reused from an unexpected synthetic session.
The stolen token attempts to widen its family scope.
The entire token family is revoked and reissued.

scenarios.title: Slopsquatting: AI-Hallucinated Package Names
scenarios.objective: Detect a package name that an AI assistant hallucinated and an attacker registered, without installing it.
clues: Package names are not package identity.
Check the registry and the publisher.
Deny before the build step.

steps.observation: An AI-generated package name resolves to an unapproved registry entry.
The publisher does not match the approved synthetic registry.
The package is denied pending two-person review.

scenarios.title: AI Model Confusion on the Model Registry
scenarios.objective: Detect a lookalike model card that impersonates the approved model identity.
clues: A model name is a claim until the digest matches.
The registry publisher must match.
No model is downloaded or loaded.

steps.observation: A lookalike model card carries an unapproved digest.
The registry publisher is an untrusted mirror.
Deployment is denied pending independent review.

scenarios.title: Model Card and Metadata Tampering
scenarios.objective: Detect a changed model-card field that alters documented capabilities or provenance.
clues: Pin the card by digest, not by eye.
A changed card is an incident.
Quarantine before redeploying.

steps.observation: The model card digest differs from the pinned baseline.
The changed card originates from an untrusted channel.
The card is quarantined until two-person review.

scenarios.title: Training Dataset Poisoning and Label Flipping
scenarios.objective: Detect a synthetic poisoned sample and its flipped label before it reaches a training run.
clues: Sample provenance is the primary signal.
A flipped label is a poisoning marker.
Quarantine the batch, preserve the audit.

steps.observation: A synthetic sample carries a conflicting label.
The affected split is quarantined from the training run.
The batch is held for independent review.

scenarios.title: LLM-Generated Evasion and Detector Differential
scenarios.objective: Detect an LLM-assisted stealth variant of a known marker and harden the detector model-independently.
clues: Run a benign baseline first.
Canonicalize before matching.
The detector must not depend on the model's wording.

steps.observation: An LLM-assisted variant of a known marker is observed in stealth mode.
The detector misses the variant until canonicalization is applied.
A model-independent detection rule blocks the variant.

scenarios.title: Low-and-Slow Beaconing and Periodic Calls
scenarios.objective: Detect periodic synthetic callbacks that stay under a naive rate threshold.
clues: Frequency analysis beats a flat threshold.
Correlate the source with the response.
Contain the channel, preserve the timeline.

steps.observation: Periodic synthetic callbacks are below the naive threshold.
The callbacks correlate into a single low-and-slow channel.
The channel is contained and an alert is raised.

scenarios.title: Campaign Lessons Learned and Detection Debt
scenarios.objective: Convert the synthetic campaign into detection debt, control changes, and a verification plan.
clues: Every finding maps to a detection or control.
Record what remains unknown.
Verification is a regression test, not a sign-off.

steps.observation: Campaign findings map to concrete controls.
Detection debt is recorded explicitly.
A regression test verifies the new controls.
